payload.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

ambiguities: Whether the set of maximizers is expected to be discrete points or an interval (the question asks 'for which real numbers x' but does not specify structure)
Whether 'maximal' means achieving a global maximum over all real x (standard interpretation) versus a local maximum
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: A maximum (not only a supremum) is assumed to exist over all real x
The expression is interpreted as a finite sum with integer index k from 1 to n
The ordering of optimization is with respect to x only, with n treated as a fixed parameter

domain_restrictions: n is an integer greater than 1
k is an integer with 1 less than or equal to k and k less than or equal to n
floor is the greatest integer less than or equal to its real argument
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each integer n greater than 1, consider the function E(n,x) = floor(n x) minus the sum from k = 1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k. Determine all real x that maximize E(n,x) among all real x, and determine the maximal value M(n) such that E(n,x) is less than or equal to M(n) for all real x, with equality for the maximizing x.
quantifier_order: Let n be an integer greater than 1 (fixed parameter)
There exists a real x* (maximizer) depending on n

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter in the optimization problem

variables.name: x
variables.role: optimization variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index running from 1 to n

witness_dependencies: The maximizing real number x* may depend on n
